quiz.instructions: Use constant-acceleration models and SI units unless another unit is requested. Give exact answers unless a rounding instruction is stated. Deceleration is a positive magnitude; signed velocity depends on the chosen direction. Where a question has several parts, choose the option with every part correct.

questions.title: 2A Q1
questions.prompt: A particle moves in a straight line with constant acceleration \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). At time \(t=0\) its speed is \(2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find its speed at \(6\,\mathrm{s}\).
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2A, Question 1; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 9; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 1 (Exercise A, Question 1).

questions.title: 2A Q3
questions.prompt: A car approaching traffic lights is travelling at \(10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Braking brings it to rest with constant deceleration in \(16\,\mathrm{s}\). Modelling the car as a particle, find its deceleration.
questions.working:
Take the initial direction of motion as positive. From \(v=u+at\),

\[0=10+16a,\qquad a=-0.625\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}.\]

Deceleration is the positive magnitude: \(0.625\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\).
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2A, Question 3; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 9; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 3 (Exercise A, Question 3).

questions.title: 2A Q5
questions.prompt: A car accelerates uniformly along a straight road between signposts \(360\,\mathrm{m}\) apart. It takes \(15\,\mathrm{s}\) to travel between them and passes the second at \(28\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find its speed at the first signpost.
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2A, Question 5; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 9; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 5 (Exercise A, Question 5).

questions.title: 2A Q7
questions.prompt: A cyclist travels along a straight road from A to B with constant acceleration \(0.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Her speed at A is \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and the journey takes \(12\,\mathrm{s}\). Find (a) her speed at B and (b) the distance AB.

questions.title: 2A Q9
questions.prompt: A particle moves from A to B in a straight line with constant deceleration \(1.2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). The journey takes \(6\,\mathrm{s}\); its speed at B is \(2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and its direction has not changed. Find (a) its speed at A and (b) the distance AB.

questions.title: 2A Q10
questions.prompt: A train slows down on a straight track with constant deceleration \(0.6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). It passes a signal at \(72\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}\) and a second signal \(25\,\mathrm{s}\) later. Find (a) its speed at the second signal in km/h and (b) the distance between the signals.

questions.title: 2A Q13
questions.prompt: A particle moves from A through B to C with constant acceleration. Its speeds at A, B and C are \(2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), \(7\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(11\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). It takes \(20\,\mathrm{s}\) from A to B. Find (a) its acceleration, (b) the time from B to C and (c) the distance AC.
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2A, Question 13; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 10; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF pages 13–14 (Exercise A, Question 13).

questions.title: 2A Q14
questions.prompt: A particle moves along a straight line from A to B with constant acceleration \(1.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\), then from B to C with a different constant acceleration. Its speeds at A and C are \(1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(43\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The two stages take \(12\,\mathrm{s}\) and \(10\,\mathrm{s}\). Find (a) its speed at B, (b) its acceleration from B to C and (c) the distance AC.
questions.working:
(a) \(v_B=1+1.5(12)=19\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

(b) \(a_{BC}=\frac{43-19}{10}=2.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\).

(c) Calculate each stage separately; the accelerations differ.

\[AB=\frac{1+19}{2}(12)=120\,\mathrm{m}.\]

\[BC=\frac{19+43}{2}(10)=310\,\mathrm{m}.\]

Therefore \(AC=120+310=430\,\mathrm{m}\).
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2A, Question 14; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 10; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF pages 15–16 (Exercise A, Question 14).

questions.title: 2A Q15
questions.prompt: A cyclist accelerates uniformly from rest to \(5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) in \(20\,\mathrm{s}\) with acceleration \(x\) m/s². She then decelerates uniformly to rest with deceleration \(\frac{x}{2}\) m/s². Find (a) the value of \(x\) and (b) the total distance travelled.
questions.working:
(a) \(5=0+20x\), so \(x=0.25\).

(b) The first stage covers \(\frac{0+5}{2}(20)=50\,\mathrm{m}\).

The second stage has acceleration \(-0.125\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\), so its duration is \(5/0.125=40\,\mathrm{s}\).

Its distance is \(\frac{5+0}{2}(40)=100\,\mathrm{m}\). Total distance: \(50+100=150\,\mathrm{m}\).
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2A, Question 15; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 10; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 17 (Exercise A, Question 15).

questions.title: 2A Q16
questions.prompt: A particle passes A, B and C in a straight line with constant acceleration at speeds \(20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), \(30\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(45\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The times AB and BC are \(t_1\) and \(t_2\). Find (a) the ratio \(\frac{t_1}{t_2}\) and (b) the distance AB if the total time AC is \(50\,\mathrm{s}\).
